title.narrative: Improved Integration of Women in the Armed Forces in the Western Balkans through increasing gender awareness and revision of military education curricula

description.narrative: This component builds upon the results achieved in raising gender awareness of the military in the first Phase of the Project. Diverse activities are planned to contribute to a more gender-sensitive organizational culture, free from obstacles to meaningful integration of women in the defence system. The Project will further strengthen the Regional Network of Gender Trainers established in the first Phase through regional meetings and support for regional cooperation and knowledge exchange. comment.narrative: Increased participation of women in the military.

Increased participation of women in the Armed Forces in the Western Balkans.
Comparative data from 2012 to 2023 show an increase in the share of women among uniformed personnel in the MoDs and AFs in BiH, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia. Specifically, there was an increase from a range of 3.3% to 6.10% in 2012 to a much higher range of 9.07% to 11.64% in 2023. This positive trend demonstrates the positive impact of the collective efforts at the regional level in the last ten years on the share of women in uniform.

title.narrative: Increased regional cooperation and strengthen capacities of Ministries of Defence to integrate gender perspective in defence policy

description.narrative: The regional platform established in the Project's first Phase (2012 – 2016) that enabled information sharing and knowledge exchange resulted in increased regional cooperation, strengthening capacities of the MoDs and AFs for gender mainstreaming, and practical solutions for gender mainstreaming in the military. The work under this component contributes to I) institutionalization of gender equality through continued support to the GEM in the MoDs; ii) increased gender-responsive policymaking and implementation capacities of Human Resources (HR) Departments in the MoDs; and iii) enhanced response to gender-based discrimination by strengthening the internal complaints mechanisms. This is done through information sharing, knowledge exchange and learning grounded in regional meetings and support for the implementation of small-scale projects.
